where: first line of the page: 'deduit de l'homomorphisme canonique f : A -> P est surjectif'
note: The TeX keeps the printed reading. P is an extension of the abelian scheme A (4.12), so the canonical homomorphism is the projection P -> A; it induces Pic(A) -> Pic(P) (4.12.2), and both 'L ≃ f*(M)' with M on A and 'si L = f*(M) est ample, il en est de même de M' further down require f : P -> A.

where: line after the display: 'où M est un Module inversible sur M.'
scan: où M est un Module inversible sur M. (both M underlined)
note: The TeX keeps the printed reading. M is an invertible Module on A: f*(M) is its pull-back to P, and Proposition 4.13 says 'M est un Module inversible ample sur A'.

scan: 𝕃* ≃ f*(M) ,  (star after the double-struck L)
note: The TeX keeps the printed star. A star after L has no meaning here (in this volume a star on a group denotes the dual), and the same relation is written 'L = f*(M)' four lines below. Probably a typing slip anticipating f*; apply the correction only if the coordinator agrees.

where: '(qui, en vertu de 4.7, peut d'ailleurs se décrire ... sur (P,P) qui sont symétriques. Il s'impose'
scan: the parenthesis opened before 'qui, en vertu de 4.7' is never closed
note: The TeX keeps the unclosed parenthesis; the parenthetical clause ends with this sentence.

where: proof of 5.1, first sentence: 'tout torseur E sous G_S est représentable'
note: The TeX keeps G_S. No G is defined here: the sentence concerns torsors under Z_S (the parenthesis extends the lemma to every separated, locally finitely presented, locally quasi-finite group scheme, and the next sentence goes on with Z_S).

scan: fidèlité (grave accent on the first e)
note: Spelling slip of the typescript (the word is 'fidélité'); the TeX keeps it.

where: 'le fait que H^1(S,Z_S) -> H^1(eta,Z_eta)) est injectif'
scan: H¹(η,Z_η)) with a surplus closing parenthesis
note: The TeX keeps the surplus parenthesis.

where: line after the display H^1(k,Z) = Hom cont(pi,Z)/Z = e: 'puisque E est sans torsion'
note: The TeX keeps E. The torsion-free group is Z (5.1): Hom cont(pi,Z) is trivial because pi is profinite and Z is torsion-free; E is the torsor.

where: Corollaire 5.2: 'le foncteur E -> E_eta de la catégorie des torseurs sur P_eta de groupe Z_{P_eta} dans la catégorie des torseurs'
scan: catégorie des torseurs sur P_η de groupe Z_{P_η} dans la catégorie des torseurs (p. 280 goes on: 'sur P_η de groupe Z_{P_η}')
note: The TeX keeps the printed reading. E -> E_eta goes from the torsors on P under Z_P to the torsors on P_eta under Z_{P_eta}; the print names the generic-fibre category as both source and target.

where: end of the proof of 5.2: 'le point générique p_i de P_i est aussi point générique de P_i .'
note: The TeX keeps P_i. As printed the clause is tautological; 5.1 is applied to the P_i and to the P_{i eta}, and the point is that both have the same generic point p_i.
